checked_claims: Giuseppe Verdi is composer; Salvadore Cammarano is librettist; Il trovatore is in four parts.
The world premiere was at Rome's Teatro Apollo on 19 January 1853.
The literary source is Antonio García Gutiérrez's drama El trovador, performed in Madrid in 1836.
Cammarano died in 1852 and Leone Emanuele Bardare made later requested additions and changes.
The character and plot explanation correctly distinguishes Manrico, the Count di Luna, Leonora, and Azucena; named musical numbers are supported.
items.distractor_review: Puccini, Rossini, and Wagner are all composers but none composed Il trovatore; the wording asks only who wrote its music, so there is one best answer.

checked_claims: Giacomo Puccini composed Tosca; Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa wrote the libretto from Victorien Sardou's drama.
The premiere was at Rome's Teatro Costanzi on 14 January 1900; the archive records 1896–99 and three acts.
Puccini saw Sardou's play with Sarah Bernhardt in 1889 and returned to sustained composition and orchestration from 1898.
The action is set in Rome in June 1800 and moves through Sant'Andrea della Valle, Palazzo Farnese, and Castel Sant'Angelo.
The article correctly separates story setting and locations from the opera's premiere date and theatre.
items.distractor_review: Verdi, Rossini, and Bizet are all composers but none composed Tosca; the direct composer wording has one best answer.
